transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

My thoughts jump all over the place and I can’t keep a straight line when I talk or plan anything anymore. It just feels like my mind is constantly ricocheting from one thing to another, and I can't seem to finish a single task or even a conversation.
Have you always struggled with this difficulty focusing since you were a child, or is this a new problem that has developed more recently?

No, this is completely new and incredibly frustrating, as I used to be highly organized and focused during my career as a museum curator. These struggles with my mind jumping around and losing focus only started about ten months ago, after I retired to care for my mother.
Besides these racing thoughts, do you ever feel like you are hearing voices that others cannot hear, or do you have the sense that people are talking about you or watching you?

Yes, it's terrifying—several times a day, especially at night when I'm sorting my mom's pills, I hear a man and a woman in the next room clearly criticizing how I'm handling everything. I've also become convinced that my neighbors and the museum board are using the local arts newsletter and clues on the train to coordinate against me and judge my caregiving, even though my niece insists they're just worried.
During these past ten months, have you also experienced significant periods where your mood was extremely low, or conversely, unusually high and energetic?

Yes, I've swung between both extremes. I have periods where I feel bizarrely amped up, giddy, and buzzing with restless energy to race around doing projects without sleeping. Then I'll crash into weeks where I feel completely flat and drained, just sitting in my robe staring at the wall with no energy to even get dressed or return calls.

During those periods when your mood is extremely low or unusually high, do you experience the voices and the sense that people are watching you at the same time, or do these experiences happen even when your mood is relatively stable?

Yes, both actually happen. In the spring, when I was completely amped up, barely sleeping, and racing to plan a festival, I heard those voices and felt watched at the exact same time. But then in late summer, when my mood was just flat and drained, those voices and the paranoia still went on for weeks without any high energy at all.

When you experienced those low or high mood periods, were the voices and paranoid thoughts specifically focused on themes related to your mood, such as feelings of failure when you were low or grandiosity when you were high?

No, the themes actually didn't change at all depending on my mood. Whether I was completely amped up or feeling totally flat and drained, the voices always criticized how I handled my mother's care, and I remained convinced the museum board and neighbors were plotting to judge me. It always came back to those same fears of being watched and criticized, regardless of how much energy I had.
Can you tell me if you have ever experienced these same voices or paranoid thoughts during a period of at least two weeks where your mood was entirely normal and stable?

Yes, that did happen. During a long stretch in late summer, my mood wasn't high or manic at all—it actually felt flat and drained—but I was still hearing those voices commenting on me and remained convinced that my neighbors and the museum board were coordinating against me.
